officials: As of 2026-11-02, 119th Congress. Roster status is taken from the House Clerk member data file (published 2026-10-01) and the Senate senators XML (last updated 2026-10-08); changes after those dates were not checked. No predictions about the 2026-11-03 election.

This section lists 23 Members: 3 Senators, 18 Representatives and 2 Delegates. CRS R48535 (May 21, 2025) counts 24 Members of Asian, South Asian or Pacific Islander ancestry (21 in the House including 3 Delegates; 3 Senators) and APAICS (Nov 2024) says '24 AA & NH/PIs in Congress overall'. Neither names the Members, and no fetched page states the heritage of the third Delegate (Guam), so that person is left out rather than inferred; the list is therefore one short of the published count. Each entry's basis cites the source that names that person.

The current edition of CRS 97-398 (Asian Pacific Americans in the United States Congress) is dated June 12, 2013 (113th Congress); it names heritage for Bera, Chu, Duckworth, Hirono, Meng, Scott and Takano and is cited only for them. CRS has not issued a newer edition that names 119th Congress Members.
CAPAC chair emerita Judy Chu wrote on 2024-12-04 that CAPAC expected 25 AAPI members of Congress in the 119th Congress; CRS and APAICS count 24. No fetched source identifies a 25th person.

Considered and not included: Yassamin Ansari (D-AZ-3), whose official bio says she is the 'first Iranian American Democrat' in Congress, and Stephanie Bice (R-OK-5), whose official pages fetched do not state heritage. Neither is shown to be counted as AA/NHPI by the CRS or APAICS figures above (the CRS and APAICS figures do not name Members). CAPAC Executive Board and Associate members who are allies (for example Ed Case, Dan Goldman, Al Green) are in capacMembers but not in officials.

Two entries have weaker heritage sourcing: Vince Fong (NBC News 2024; no official, CRS, APAICS or CAPAC page naming his heritage was retrieved) and Kimberlyn King-Hinds (Pew text hosted on her official site). Reviewers should confirm these before citing. Guam's Delegate James C. Moylan is not listed because no fetched source states his heritage.
Senate member pages (senate.gov) and congress.gov/bioguide HTML pages block automated fetching, so Senators' heritage rests on CRS 97-398, H. Doc. 108-226 and APAICS, not on their senate.gov bios.

bodies: All records built from pages fetched on 2026-11-02. The shared WebSearch budget ran out mid-task, so bodies not found before that point (see next notes) were left out rather than guessed.

Only Interior's Office of Native Hawaiian Relations was confirmed at federal agency level.

Status wording: 'active' means a fetched page dated or live in 2025-2026 shows the body operating. 'unclear' means the body exists in fetched sources but the latest evidence is older or undated (dates given in x). Several legislative caucuses are 'unclear' for that reason, not because they are known to have ended.

funding: Part 1 (EINs): candidates came from the ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer API and the IRS Exempt Organizations Business Master File (eo1-eo4 CSVs, fetched 2026-11-02). 'conf' shows the evidence: 'site-printed EIN' = the organization's own website prints the same EIN; 'name+city/state' = IRS name and city/state match the directory; 'name (directory has no HQ city)' = exact name only; 'none' = no EIN assigned (see x).

Government bodies (CAPAC, OHA, WA and CA commissions, DHHL, ONHR) are skipped by instruction. Smithsonian APAC, UCLA AASC and UC Berkeley AARC are typed non-government in the directory but have no IRS record under their names, so ein is null.
'arms' lists a second legal entity (e.g. 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(4) counterpart) and 'sponsor' a fiscal sponsor; 'unverified': true marks a link or identity the sources fetched do not settle.

Part 2 (grants): parsed from IRS e-file XML (Form 990 Schedule I RecipientTable; Form 990-PF Part XV grants paid during the year) downloaded from the IRS TEOS bulk files at apps.irs.gov. Each 'u' is the ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer full-filing page for the same IRS object id ('oid'); the page loads its schedules with JavaScript, so open Schedule I or the 990-PF statement from its menu.

'yr' is the calendar year in which the funder's fiscal year ended; 'fye' gives the exact period end date. Fiscal years differ: Kellogg ends Aug, Weingart June, California Endowment March (one filing ends Dec 2024), Carnegie Sept.

Coverage is limited to filings the IRS released in 2024-2026 (fiscal years ending 2023-2025). Earlier years were not parsed. 244 matching grant lines were found; 102 were kept: all 32 TAAF Schedule I lines to directory organizations, plus the largest or most informative lines per funder. Small payments (under $5,000) were left out.

Matching rules: Schedule I lines matched on the recipient EIN printed in the filing. Form 990-PF lines carry no recipient EIN, so they were matched on name AND city/state; same-name lines with another city were dropped (e.g. an AAJA line at a San Francisco address in a Ford filing; a Wallace line for CAPACD at an Oakland address; branch-level Boat People SOS and JACL chapter grants).

'recipient' is copied exactly from the filing, including typos and truncations (e.g. 'AMERCIAN' in Kellogg lines, a cut-off name in an Open Society line). 'purpose' is as stated, cut to 120 characters with '...' where longer. A fiscally sponsored recipient appears under the sponsor's name (Weingart: 'Community Partners FBO Empowering Pacific Islander Communities').

Silicon Valley Community Foundation is a community foundation; its filing does not say which lines were donor-advised, so treat those lines as SVCF grants without further attribution. Foundation to Promote Open Society is the Open Society Foundations entity whose 990-PF was parsed; other OSF entities were not checked.

No grant line matched in the parsed filings for these directory ids: stop-aapi-hate, jacl, asian-american-scholar-forum, aapi-data, potluck-asian-america, apapa, saalt, hindu-american-foundation, vietaid, boat-people-sos, hmong-national-development, aapi-victory-fund, chinese-american-citizens-alliance, smithsonian-asian-pacific-american-center, nextshark, south-asian-journalists-association, ucla-asian-american-studies-center, uc-berkeley-asian-american-research-center, napca, apala, nqapia, aapcho. Absence is not proof: other funders, earlier years, and fiscal-sponsor or chapter names were not searched. AAPIP's own filings show no grants to directory organizations.
ProPublica blocks scripted PDF and XML downloads with a security check, so the IRS bulk XML was the source; page images/PDFs were not read.
